classification.difficultyReason: Translate labelled roots into factors with opposite signs, then use their midpoint and substitution to find the turning point.

content.prompt:
These equations are of the form $y=(x+\alpha)(x+\beta)$.
Use the $x$-intercepts to find the values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$, then find the coordinates of the turning point.

spec.description: Upward parabola with labelled x-intercepts 1 and 3; no grid or additional numerical labels.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible; its equation and turning-point coordinates are answers only.

answer.worked:
The intercepts give $y=(x-1)(x-3)$, so $\alpha=-1$ and $\beta=-3$, in either order.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{TP}}&=\frac{1+3}{2}=2\\y_{\mathrm{TP}}&=(2-1)(2-3)\\y_{\mathrm{TP}}&=-1\end{align*}$$
Turning point: $(2,-1)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with labelled x-intercepts -5 and 1; turning point below the x-axis and left of the y-axis.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph only; equation and turning-point coordinates hidden in question editions.

answer.worked:
The intercepts give $y=(x+5)(x-1)$, so $\alpha=5$ and $\beta=-1$, in either order.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{TP}}&=\frac{-5+1}{2}=-2\\y_{\mathrm{TP}}&=(-2+5)(-2-1)\\y_{\mathrm{TP}}&=-9\end{align*}$$
Turning point: $(-2,-9)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with labelled x-intercepts -2 and 6; turning point below the x-axis and right of the y-axis.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph only; equation and turning-point coordinates are answer content.

answer.worked:
The intercepts give $y=(x+2)(x-6)$, so $\alpha=2$ and $\beta=-6$, in either order.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{TP}}&=\frac{-2+6}{2}=2\\y_{\mathrm{TP}}&=(2+2)(2-6)\\y_{\mathrm{TP}}&=-16\end{align*}$$
Turning point: $(2,-16)$.
